items.title: 281 lawyers apply for Senior Advocate designation under Madras High Court's new Rules
items.summary: 281 lawyers practicing before the Madras High Court have applied for Senior Advocate designation under a substantially revamped designation regime. The High Court on October 6 published the list of applicants and invited suggestions or views from practising advocates, the Bar Council and relevant bar associations. The views must be supported by verifiable material and should be submitted to the Registrar (Administration) by 5.45 pm on October 27. The list runs to 281 applicants, with enrolment years ranging from the 1970s to 2015. The exercise comes nearly four years after the High Court's previous round of designations. In January 2023, the full court of the High Court designated 62 lawyers as Senior Advocates under the then-existing 2020 Rules. The present exercise, however, is being conducted under the Rules for Designation of Senior Advocates by the High Court of Madras, 2026. The news Rules were notified on July 23 this year. The new Rules were framed against the backdrop of a May 2025 Supreme Court judgment that discarded the earlier 100-point assessment system for Senior Advocate designations and directed High Courts to amend or substitute their existing rules. items.title: Bombay High Court holds two lawyers guilty of contempt for threatening trial judge, slaps ₹1 lakh costs
items.summary: The Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court recently convicted two lawyers for criminal contempt of court for shouting at a trial judge and threatening him in open court [ Sajiduzzaman Mhammad Hanif Shahid v. Sagar Rathod & Anr. ]. A Bench of Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D Wakode ruled that threatening judicial officers and shouting inside a courtroom constituted grave misconduct. Obstruction in the judicial process by lawyers cannot be tolerated under any circumstances, the Court underscored. “Interference in the administration of justice by giving threats, addressing the judicial officer in loud voice and prohibiting him from passing orders are definitely serious acts. More so, when such acts have been done by an advocate who is the officer of the Court, he should promote and see that all others who are present should also maintain the decorum of the Court. Obstruction in judicial process by an advocate cannot be tolerated,” the Court held. items.title: Gurvinder Pal Singh sworn in as additional judge; Delhi High Court working strength rises to 50 judges
items.summary: Judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh was sworn into office as an additional judge of the Delhi High Court this morning. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre administered the oath of office to Justice Gurvinder Pal Singh. With Justice Singh's appointment, the Delhi High Court's working strength has risen to 50 judges, against its sanctioned strength of 60, leaving 10 vacancies. The Central government had notified the appointment of Justice Singh as an additional judge on October 5. The appointment came nearly a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended Singh's appointment as a High Court judge on September 10. In its September 10 statement, the Collegium had recommended eight judicial officers (including Singh) for appointment as judges of the Delhi High Court. Seven of these names were cleared by the Central government on September 19 . Justice Singh's elevation as a High Court judge was notified thereafter by the Centre on October 5.

items.title: Calcutta High Court awards ₹5.36 lakh compensation to man who continued to be imprisoned for 60 days after bail
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court recently ordered the West Bengal government to pay ₹ 5.36 lakh as compensation to a tea garden worker who continued to be detained in police custody for 60 additional days after he was supposed to be released on bail. A Division Bench comprising Justices Debangsu Basak and Aryak Dutt passed the ruling on a habeas corpus petition seeking the accused worker’s release. “We hold the period of detention of the writ petitioner between August 6, 2018 and October 5, 2018 was not sanctioned by law. The writ petitioner, therefore, is entitled to compensation for such period,” the October 5 ruling said. Justices Debangsu Basak, Aryak Dutt The worker (petitioner) had been booked in three criminal cases, but had secured bail in all of them and was supposed to be released from jail on August 6, 2018. However, he was not immediately released, prompting him to file a petition before the High Court for release. He was later released on October 5, 2018, around 2 months after he was supposed to be released on bail. items.title: Allahabad High Court applies US doctrine of 'fruit of poisonous tree' to release accused arrested after illegal detention
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently ordered release of an accused who was formally arrested by the police on September 16 only after keeping him under illegal detention for 31 hours [Ravi Chaurasiya And Another v State of UP and 4 others] A bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdeva found that the police formally arrested the accused Ravi Chaurasiya only after his mother approached the High Court with a habeas corpus petition. Prior to that, he was being kept in illegal detention. “The police cannot be permitted to legitimize an arrest, where it was subsequent to an act of unlawful detention. The subsequent arrest memo and the remand does not legitimize the initial unlawful detention of the corpus. Therefore, where the initial action of unlawful detention itself was violative of the right of the corpus under Article 22, the same cannot be set right by a subsequent action of the police by formally arresting the corpus on 16.09.2026 at 10.45 am,” the Court ruled. The Court rejected the police claim that they forgot to make an entry in the General Diary for Chaurasiya's custody for more than 24 hours. items.title: Bulli Bai case: Mumbai Court discharges accused Vishal Jha; says merely following mobile app no offence
items.summary: A Mumbai court has closed the case Vishal Sudhirkumar Jha in the Bulli Bai app case in which photographs of over 100 Muslim women were displayed for an auction [Vishal Jha v. State of Maharashtra] The judicial magistrate at Bandra RT Ingle passed the order on October 6. The magistrate highlighted the lack of direct involvement of Jha and ruled that merely being in contact with co-accused does not automatically establish liability for their criminal acts. “May be the applicant has followed Bullibai App due to his familiarity with the co-accused and contact with them, but, in entire charge-sheet there is no further role of the present applicant which would show that, he either created said App or the help co-accused in creating it,” the judge said. The judge also relied on an Allahabad High Court precedent to establish that simply following a page on a website is not a punishable offence. The case revolves around an application hosted on GitHub that unlawfully displayed photographs of over 100 Muslim women for an intended auction. Justice A Badharudeen dismissed the convict's appeal against a June 2024 trial court verdict convicting him of rape, aggravated penetrative sexual assault and other offences under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act). The appellant had primarily challenged his conviction by pointing to omissions and variations in the child survivor's testimony. However, the Court observed that the testimony was of sterling quality and supported by medical evidence. The move came after Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader and former Industries Minister TRB Rajaa criticised the use of Hindi on the covers, saying it appeared that a three-language policy was being implemented in government hospitals. Similar covers had also been used at the Government Medical College Hospital in Karur, which has also stopped using them. According to CMCH resident medical officer B Saravanapriya, the covers were not newly introduced and had been in use for more than 18 months, including under the previous government. “These covers are being printed at Chinthamani Cooperative Society with funds from sponsors,” she told The Times of India. items.title: Delhi High Court says PepsiCo, Monster can sell existing stocks of "energy drinks" but can't make more
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday said that PepsiCo and Monster Beverages can sell their existing stocks of beverages labelled as “Energy Drink”, but cannot manufacture any more products bearing the descriptor. While PepsiCo manufactures Sting Energy and Adrenaline Rush, Monster sells its product under the name Monster Energy. They had approached the High Court against orders passed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) directing them to drop the label "energy drink". The FSSAI had also directed the food safety officers across India to seize the products. Justice Amit Mahajan today said that he is staying the order to the extent that no coercive action will be taken against the companies. However, the Court added that it does not mean that the companies can continue manufacturing more products with the label. The order will stay in force till the next date of hearing on November 5. " Your existing stock will be sold," the Court added. Justice Amit Mahajan The High Court passed the order while dealing with the petitions filed by PepsiCo and Monster Beverages. items.title: Hyderabad BJP BLA booked over attempt to delete 30 Muslim voters using Form 7
items.summary: A BJP booth-level agent, S Balachander, has been booked in Hyderabad for allegedly attempting to delete 30 Muslim voters from the electoral rolls using pre-printed Form 7 applications. The Chikkadpally police registered the case on October 6 after election officials found that all 30 voters were living at the addresses recorded in the electoral rolls. The case was based on a complaint by T Praveen Kumar, Electoral Registration Officer of the Musheerabad Assembly constituency and Deputy Commissioner of GHMC Circle 41. Police booked Balachander under sections 217 (false information with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to the injury of another person) and 318(2) (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. According to the complaint, Balachander brought 30 digitally pre-printed Form 7 applications to polling station No. 210 in Surya Nagar, Chikkadpally, on September 28. items.title: Voter turnout in TN’s Madurantakam and Dharapuram bye-polls drop
items.summary: Voter turnout in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu dipped significantly in the bye-elections held on October 6, compared to the Assembly polls five months ago. According to the figures reported by the Election Commission of India (ECI) website at 9 pm on the day, Madurantakam recorded an approximate turnout of 86.26%, against 93.22% in the Assembly election, with a drop of nearly 7%. Dharapuram recorded 80.30% polling, compared to 89.89% in the Assembly election, indicating a decline of nearly 9.5 percent The bye-elections were necessitated after the sitting MLAs, who had won the seats on All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) tickets in the Assembly election, subsequently switched to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). For the bye-elections, TVK fielded the same two candidates. The bye-elections were held as a five-cornered contest between the ruling TVK, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), AIADMK, and Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK). Left parties, despite their post-poll alliance with the TVK, fielded their own candidates. items.title: Nandini milk may cost up to Rs 8 more per litre from November 1
items.summary: Nandini milk is set to become costlier by up to Rs 8 per litre after the Karnataka Cabinet approved a price hike on October 6, but held back its announcement due to the Model Code of Conduct (MCC). The government will seek the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) approval before implementing the hike, with Chief Minister DK Shivakumar authorised to take the final call on the extent of the increase. The revised prices are likely to come into effect from November 1, subject to ECI clearance. If the full Rs 8 increase is passed on to consumers, Nandini toned milk, sold in the blue packet, will cost Rs 54 per litre, up from the current Rs 46. Of the proposed Rs 8 increase, Rs 6 is expected to go to milk producers and Rs 2 to milk unions. The hike comes after milk unions sought an increase of Rs 8 to Rs 10 per litre, citing rising costs of cattle feed, fodder, medicines, transportation and plastic packaging. They also pointed to fodder shortages caused by the drought and Karnataka’s lower milk procurement price compared to neighbouring states. A division bench of Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice KS Bharath Kumar directed the State to pay the costs to the Advocates Clerks Association and produce the receipt along with its statement of objections. “There is absolutely no justification on the part of the respondents-State in not filing the objections in spite of repeated time being granted,” the Court observed. The Court further said that once a PIL is taken cognizance of and the State is directed to file its response, the government's affidavit must be placed on record.
